names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 14 Απριλίου, «Άγιος Αρδαλίων ο Μίμος», with the rank word and the epithet left off; the life page heads him «Αγιος Αρδαλιων ο Μιμος (; - 298)».

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue's third heading for the Julian 14 April on pravoslavno.rs, „Св. муч. Ардалион Глумац.“, with Св. left off — it is not a rank — and with муч. left off as well, the rank word this source uses for a martyr, which this folder already carries in `types`. **Глумац is kept**: it is not a rank word in `BRIEF-SERBIAN.md` §5's table but the trade the entry's whole account turns on, the player of parts, and it is the by-name this folder's own English display name carries as «the Mime». This is also the folder's second name form of any kind: it held only the Greek Αρδαλίων.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 14ης Απριλίου — «Άγιος Αρδαλίων ο Μίμος»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 14 Απριλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. It gives him no city and no judge by name, no relic, and no hymn. The corpus holds nobody else of this name; the only other mime it keeps is Porphyrius the Mime (15 September), a different man on a different day. The day's line calls him ο Μίμος and the body of the page glosses the word: «με τη σημερινή ορολογία ήταν ηθοποιός» — in today's wording, an actor.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 27.04.2026 (14. април ст. ст.) — „Св. муч. Ардалион Глумац.“

attestations.note: The day's third entry, on the same menologion day the Greek keeps him on; the Russian and Romanian rows stay `undocumented`. The man is the same beyond doubt: the actor who played the martyr for the crowd's amusement and then became one. **No date was touched and none was added**: this folder holds `death` 298 off saint.gr's heading «(; - 298)» and its «στα χρόνια του Διοκλητιανού (298)», and **the Prologue names the persecution under Maximian instead and prints no year at all** — so there is nothing to add and nothing to displace, and the difference of emperor is recorded here. New to the folder: that he was a **comedian**, and that **of all parts he liked best to play the martyr for the faith, mocking the Christians in every way he could**; that **when the persecution came his spirit was entirely changed**; that he **cried out aloud before the people that he was a Christian and was not joking**; and that he was **tied to a white-hot iron grid and died on it, having played at last the true and honourable part of a martyr** — which is the entry's own closing figure. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion, and this folder has no hymn from any source. The stored form keeps the by-name Глумац and folds with nothing.
